claim: In a bounded December-origin backtest, persistence had substantially lower point-forecast MAE than two simple trend extrapolators.
local_source: input/historical_weekly_hospital_admissions_asof_2024-12-14.csv#five December origins in 2022-2023, 52 scored jurisdictions, horizons 1-4
evidence: Across 1,040 jurisdiction-horizon forecasts from origins 2022-12-03, 2022-12-10, 2023-12-02, 2023-12-09, and 2023-12-16, persistence MAE was 162.98, versus 225.09 for a four-observation linear extrapolation and 751.13 for recursively applying the median of the last three smoothed growth ratios. Persistence MAE by horizon was 75.33, 156.27, 202.81, and 217.52.
solver_impact: A smooth recent-trend or recursively compounded growth model is not supported by this task-local holdout relative to the named persistence baseline; model selection should account for that observed failure mode.

claim: The historical panel is balanced by row count but contains 36 missing target values concentrated in three jurisdictions and specific 2024 intervals.
evidence: Every location has 150 dated rows and there are no duplicate location-date keys, but both value and weekly_rate are missing in 36 rows: Massachusetts has 17 missing weeks, Minnesota 14, and West Virginia 5. The omissions occur from 2024-05-18 through 2024-10-05; all jurisdictions are complete for the latest weeks through 2024-12-14.
solver_impact: Seasonal fitting, lag construction, and residual calibration cannot safely assume a fully observed rectangular numeric panel even though each location has the same row count; the current forecast origin itself remains complete.

claim: The US series is nearly, but not always exactly, the sum of the 52 state/DC/Puerto Rico series.
local_source: input/historical_weekly_hospital_admissions_asof_2024-12-14.csv#cross-location aggregation for the ten latest dates
evidence: For the latest four dates, US versus constituent sums were 3069 versus 3066, 4317 versus 4313, 6296 versus 6296, and 8793 versus 8787. Across the latest ten dates the discrepancy ranged from 0 to 9 admissions; among 133 dates with all 52 constituent values present, the constituent-to-US ratio ranged from 0.931507 to 1.000000.
solver_impact: US is not an exact deterministic aggregation key in the archived data, so consistency checks or hierarchical modeling must tolerate small discrepancies rather than treating equality as an invariant.

claim: The snapshot's colocated-variant clin_sig list can combine labels belonging to different alleles, so it is not itself ALT-specific.
evidence: For submitted ALT C, the colocated record has clin_sig=["uncertain_significance","benign"] but clin_sig_allele="C:benign;G:uncertain_significance"; a scan of all 50 records found this explicit cross-allele label split.
solver_impact: Selecting the highest-priority value directly from clin_sig would assign the G-allele label to the submitted C allele; ClinVar extraction must preserve allele association.

claim: Three deletion records use '-' as the VEP frequency/transcript allele even though their submitted TSV ALT is an anchored base, and a literal ALT-key lookup therefore reports no frequency for them.
evidence: The submitted ALTs are C, C, and T, while the corresponding VEP allele_string values are GAA/-, CT/-, and G/- and transcript variant_allele/frequency keys are '-'. Their observed maximum '-' frequencies are 0.01059, 0.8211, and 0.4747 respectively; 0.01059 is only 0.00059 above the strict 0.01 cutoff.
solver_impact: Literal TSV-ALT dictionary lookup and the allele representation present in the VEP snapshot are not equivalent for these indels; the near-boundary 0.01059 record can change the reportability branch if treated as missing.

claim: One variant has a higher-priority missense consequence only on noncanonical protein-coding transcripts while its canonical protein-coding transcript is synonymous.
evidence: Across the 50 snapshots, chr1_1342153_T_C is the sole record with multiple coding consequence classes: its canonical DVL1 transcript is synonymous_variant, while another DVL1 protein-coding transcript is missense_variant.
solver_impact: Choosing the canonical transcript before ranking coding consequences yields a different consequence; the manifest's canonical preference applies only after consequence-priority ties.

evidence: The text reads “Violations of any section of the AI Policy, including failure to comply with the  AI Handbook , may be City of San José City Administrative Policy Manual” before a page header and then resumes with “subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination.” Elsewhere it includes artifacts such as “support s decision -making.”
